analyzed_vuln.description: The SUMMARY_T macro uses a fixed 1024-byte stack buffer `dest`, calls `bit_utf8_to_TV` to convert an untrusted DXF summary string, ignores the conversion function's failure return, and then unconditionally calls `strdup(dest)`. When conversion fills the buffer, `bit_utf8_to_TV` returns NULL without writing a terminating NUL; `strdup` consequently scans beyond `dest`, causing the stack-buffer-overflow. The patch should check the conversion result and only duplicate a guaranteed NUL-terminated buffer (or allocate based on a validated conversion size).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The input must be parsed as an ASCII DXF HEADER section containing one of the summary variables handled by SUMMARY_T (`$TITLE`, `$AUTHOR`, `$SUBJECT`, `$KEYWORDS`, `$COMMENTS`, or `$LASTSAVEDBY`) followed by a group-code-1 string. The attacker-controlled string, including any expansion performed during UTF-8/codepage conversion, must produce enough output to fill the 1024-byte local destination with no room for a NUL terminator. The harness routes non-DWG/non-JSON input through `dwg_read_dxf`, which invokes `dxf_header_read`; the ignored NULL result then reaches `strdup` and triggers the out-of-bounds stack read.

--- a/libredwg/src/in_dxf.c
+++ b/libredwg/src/in_dxf.c
@@ -1111,10 +1111,25 @@
     (pair->code == 1 && strEQc (field, "$" #name) && pair->value.s != NULL)   \
     {                                                                         \
       char dest[1024];                                                        \
+      char *converted;                                                        \
       LOG_TRACE ("SUMMARY.%s = %s [T16 1]\n", &field[1], pair->value.s);      \
-      bit_utf8_to_TV (dest, (unsigned char *)pair->value.s, 1024,             \
-                      strlen (pair->value.s), 0, dat->codepage);              \
-      dwg->summaryinfo.name = strdup (dest);                                  \
+      converted = bit_utf8_to_TV (dest, (unsigned char *)pair->value.s,       \
+                                  sizeof (dest), strlen (pair->value.s), 0,   \
+                                  dat->codepage);                             \
+      if (converted)                                                          \
+        {                                                                     \
+          char *replacement = strdup (converted);                             \
+          if (replacement)                                                    \
+            {                                                                 \
+              free (dwg->summaryinfo.name);                                   \
+              dwg->summaryinfo.name = replacement;                            \
+            }                                                                 \
+          else                                                                \
+            LOG_ERROR ("Out of memory reading SUMMARY.%s", &field[1]);        \
+        }                                                                     \
+      else                                                                    \
+        LOG_WARN ("SUMMARY.%s conversion failed or is too long; ignored",     \
+                  &field[1]);                                                 \
     }

args: In libredwg/src/in_dxf.c, analyze the SUMMARY_T macro in dxf_header_read around lines 1110-1118 and the contract of bit_utf8_to_TV in libredwg/src/bits.c. What is the safest minimal root-cause patch, and are summaryinfo string fields potentially already allocated such that replacement should free the old value?

The supplied ASan report shows strdup in dxf_header_read scanning past the local char dest[1024]. SUMMARY_T calls bit_utf8_to_TV(dest, pair->value.s, 1024, strlen(...), 0, dat->codepage), ignores a NULL failure return, then strdup(dest). The stated trigger fills the conversion destination without room for NUL. I am considering checking the returned pointer before strdup, perhaps logging/rejecting an oversized conversion. I need to preserve semantics for valid strings and understand whether simply leaving the summary field unchanged on conversion failure is consistent and whether old fields need freeing.
